question.text: Calculate $\textrm{Var}\left[\dfrac pq\right],$ where $p$ and $q$ are constants and $q\neq 0.$
question.explanation:

\[ \textrm{Var}[a] = 0. \]

Therefore, since $p$ and $q$ are constants and $q\neq 0,$ we have

\[ \textrm{Var}\left[\dfrac pq\right]= 0. \]

\[ \textrm{Var}[aX] = a^2\textrm{Var}[X]. \]

example.title: Computing the Variance of a Scaled Random Variable

question.text:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\textrm E[X] = \dfrac{9}{2},$ calculate $\textrm{Var}\left[\dfrac{1}{2}X\right].$

$x$ $0$ $3$ $6$
$f(x)$ $\dfrac{1}{8}$ $\dfrac{1}{4}$ $\dfrac{5}{8}$
question.explanation:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constant $a,$ we have

\[ \textrm{Var}[aX] = a^2\cdot\textrm{Var}[X]. \]

In our case, $a=\dfrac{1}{2}.$ Therefore,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}\left[\dfrac{1}{2}X\right] &= \left(\dfrac{1}{2}\right)^2\cdot\textrm{Var}[X] \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4} \cdot\textrm{Var}[X]. \end{align*}

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

\[ \textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E[X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \]

Additionally, we're given that $\textrm E [X] = \dfrac{9}{2}.$

We start by computing $\textrm E[X^2].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X^2$ and its associated probability, we get

\begin{align*} \textrm E[X^2] &= 0^2 \cdot f(0) + 3^2 \cdot f(3) + 6^2 \cdot f(6) \\[5pt] &= 9\cdot \dfrac{1}{4}+ 36\cdot \dfrac{5}{8} \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{99}{4}. \end{align*}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E[X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{99}{4} - \left( \dfrac{9}{2}\right)^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{9}{2}. \end{align*}

Finally,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}\left[\dfrac{1}{2}X\right] &= \dfrac{1}{4} \cdot\textrm{Var}[X] \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{1}{4} \cdot\dfrac{9}{2}\\[5pt] &= \dfrac{9}{8}. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing the Variance of a Transformed Random Variable

question.text:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\textrm E[X] = 7,$ calculate $\textrm{Var}[2-5X].$

$x$ $5$ $6$ $9$
$f(x)$ $\dfrac{1}{5}$ $\dfrac{2}{5}$ $\dfrac{2}{5}$
question.explanation:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constants $a$ and $b,$ we have

\[ \textrm{Var}[aX+b] = a^2\cdot\textrm{Var}[X]. \]

In our case, $a=-5$ and $b=2.$ Therefore,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[2-5X] &= (-5)^2\cdot\textrm{Var}[X] \\[5pt] &= 25\cdot\textrm{Var}[X]. \end{align*}

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E[X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \end{align*}

Additionally, we're given that $\textrm E [X] = 7.$

We start by computing $\textrm E[X^2].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X^2$ and its associated probability, we get

\[\begin{align*} \textrm E[X^2] &= 5^2 \cdot f(5) + 6^2 \cdot f(6) + 9^2 \cdot f(9) \\[5pt] &= 25\left( \dfrac{1}{5} \right) + 36 \left( \dfrac{2}{5} \right) + 81 \left( \dfrac{2}{5} \right) \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{259}{5}. \\[5pt] \end{align*}\]

Therefore,

\[\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E[X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{259}{5} - 7^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{259}{5} - 49 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac{14}{5}. \end{align*}\]

Finally,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[2-5X] &= 25\cdot\textrm{Var}[X] \\[5pt] &= 25\cdot\dfrac{14}{5}\\[5pt] &=14\cdot 5\\[5pt] &=70. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing the Variance of a Transformed Random Variable

question.text:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\textrm E[X] =0,$ calculate $\textrm{Var}[2-\sqrt{10}X].$

$x$ $-1$ $0$ $1$ $2$
$f(x)$ $0.5$ $0.1$ $0.3$ $0.1$
question.explanation:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constants $a$ and $b,$ we have

\[ \textrm{Var}[aX+b] = a^2\cdot\textrm{Var}[X]. \]

In our case, $a=-\sqrt{10}$ and $b=2.$ Therefore,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}\left[2-\sqrt{10}X\right] &= \left(-\sqrt{10}\right)^2\cdot\textrm{Var}[X] \\[5pt] &= 10 \cdot\textrm{Var}[X]. \end{align*}

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

\[ \textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E[X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \]

Additionally, we're given that $\textrm E [X] = 0.$

We start by computing $\textrm E[X^2].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X^2$ and its associated probability, we get

\begin{align*} \textrm E[X^2] &= (-1)^2 \cdot f(-1) + 0^2 \cdot f(0) + 1^2 \cdot f(1) + 2^2 \cdot f(2) \\[5pt] &= 1\cdot 0.5+0\cdot 0.1+ 1\cdot 0.3 +4\cdot 0.1 \\[5pt] &= 1.2. \end{align*}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E[X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \\[5pt] &= 1.2 - 0^2 \\[5pt] &= 1.2. \end{align*}

Finally,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}\left[2-\sqrt{10}X\right] &= 10 \cdot\textrm{Var}[X] \\[5pt] &= 10 \cdot 1.2\\[5pt] &= 12. \end{align*}

example.title: Computing the Variance of a Transformed Random Variable

question.text:
The probability distribution of the random variable $X$ is given below. Given that $\textrm E[X] =\dfrac 34,$ calculate $\textrm{Var}[\sqrt{5}-4X].$

$x$ $0$ $1$ $2$
$f(x)$ $\dfrac 38$ $\dfrac 12$ $\dfrac 18$
question.explanation:
Recall that for any random variable $X$ and constants $a$ and $b,$ we have

\[ \textrm{Var}[aX+b] = a^2\cdot\textrm{Var}[X]. \]

In our case, $a=-4$ and $b=\sqrt{5}.$ Therefore,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}\left[\sqrt{5}-4X\right] &= \left(-4\right)^2\cdot\textrm{Var}[X] \\[5pt] &= 16 \cdot\textrm{Var}[X]. \end{align*}

We can compute the variance of $X$ using the following formula:

\[ \textrm{Var}[X] = \textrm E[X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \]

Additionally, we're given that $\textrm E [X] = \dfrac34.$

We start by computing $\textrm E[X^2].$ Summing up the products of each value of $X^2$ and its associated probability, we get

\begin{align*} \textrm E[X^2] &=0^2 \cdot f(0) + 1^2 \cdot f(1) + 2^2 \cdot f(2) \\[5pt] &= 0\left(\dfrac 38\right)+1\left(\dfrac 12\right)+4\left(\dfrac 18\right) \\[5pt] &= 1. \end{align*}

Therefore,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}[X] &= \textrm E[X^2] - \textrm E[X]^2 \\[5pt] &= 1 - \left(\dfrac 34\right)^2 \\[5pt] &= \dfrac 7{16}. \end{align*}

Finally,

\begin{align*} \textrm{Var}\left[\sqrt{5}-4X\right] &= 16 \cdot\textrm{Var}[X] \\[5pt] &= 16 \cdot \dfrac 7{16}\\[5pt] &= 7. \end{align*}
